content:
- Model consistently underestimates true values, especially in early days of the 30-day window.
- Forecast shows upward trend (increasing) while true values often dip or show volatility, suggesting overconfidence in continuation of prior trend.
- When true values spike upward (e.g., 79.14, 80.24), model fails to catch the momentum, leading to underestimation.
- Model tends to smooth out volatility, ignoring sharp drops or spikes in true data.
- Forecast often starts at a lower level than true values, suggesting a lag in capturing recent high values.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias — it overcorrects downward after spikes, missing the true continuation or reversal.
- For horizon > 10 days, model shows diminishing sensitivity to recent high values, leading to persistent underestimation.
- Model fails to adjust for sudden drops in true values (e.g., 70.01) — it doesn’t react to sharp downward corrections.
- Forecast is overly optimistic in early days, then gradually adjusts — but often too late to catch true turning points.
- Model doesn’t account for “recovery” phases after sharp drops — it assumes continuation of prior trend instead of recalibrating.
